name: fetch_url
description: Fetch an http or https URL and return the response body as text. Use to read documentation, an API response or a page whose contents the answer depends on.

url.description: The URL to fetch. Must be http or https; any other scheme is refused, so file://, ftp:// and gopher:// are not routes out of this tool.

max_bytes.description: Stop reading after this many bytes and say so. Guards against templating a whole binary into a prompt.

timeout_seconds.description: How long the whole transfer may take. Kept under the tool's own timeout so a slow host is reported as a slow host rather than as the tool dying.

accept.description: Value for the Accept header, e.g. "application/json". Sent as given, so it is also the way to ask an API for a particular representation.

output_schema.description: The response body, verbatim and undecorated, so a JSON response is still parseable JSON. A body longer than max_bytes is cut at that point and a final "[fetch_url] response truncated: ..." line is appended, which does make the result no longer parse.

exit_codes.2: invalid input (stdin was not a JSON object, or a parameter is missing or the wrong type)
exit_codes.5: unreachable (DNS failure, connection refused, TLS failure, or the transfer timed out)
exit_codes.6: http error (the server answered, with a 4xx or 5xx status)
